feed.title: P2share: how to turn any network (or testnet!) into a bitcoin miner

entry.title: P2share: how to turn any network (or testnet!) into a bitcoin miner
entry.summary:
The discussion revolves around the complexities and potential implications of innovative distributed mining mechanisms, particularly focusing on how they might be employed to coordinate major upgrades on a blockchain network, which may not be backward compatible. These mechanisms explore the theoretical bounds of maintaining fairness and preventing exploitative behaviors among participants in decentralized networks. The core idea presented is that a sharechain network could incorporate additional consensus logic that becomes active only when it achieves a majority of the mainchain hashrate. This scenario could lead to a situation where the network enforces mainchain blocks to remain essentially empty, containing merely a commitment to the upgraded network's tip and possibly a notification message indicating that a hard fork has occurred.
This hypothetical setup suggests that after gaining sufficient hashrate, the sharechain could effectively execute a 51% attack on the mainchain, albeit with potentially benevolent intentions. The security of such a system, however, hinges on the composition of its miners and mining pools, and remains at risk until possibly superseded by another superior sharechain network. This ongoing vulnerability could act as a deterrent against malicious intents, preserving a degree of integrity and benevolence in the network's operations.
Furthermore, the application of such mechanisms can swing between beneficial and detrimental outcomes, heavily dependent on the perspective and intent behind their use. In scenarios where projects aim to preserve or enhance the foundational principles of a cryptocurrency like Bitcoin, employing such a mechanism could facilitate a smoother transition by leveraging sufficient hashpower to initiate desired soft or hard forks. This approach allows these projects to validate their modifications while maintaining relevance on the mainchain during the transitional phase. Such strategic deployment underscores the dual-edged nature of technological advancements in blockchain governance and the critical balance between innovation and the maintenance of a secure, fair network infrastructure.
